learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the precise formats and appropriate tones required for communicating effectively through formal and informal letters.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Written to officials, editors, or businesses. The tone must be polite, objective, and strictly to the point. No personal gossip or slang is allowed.
1. Sender's Address -> 2. Date -> 3. Receiver's Address -> 4. Subject -> 5. Salutation (Respected Sir/Madam) -> 6. Body -> 7. Complimentary Close (Yours sincerely/faithfully) -> 8. Signature/Name.
In a formal letter, the subject line is crucial. It should be written in 4-6 words and summarize exactly why the letter is being written (e.g., Subject: Application for the post of Manager).
Written to friends and family. The tone is warm, personal, and conversational. You don't need a receiver's address or a subject line.
A specific type of formal letter written to a newspaper to highlight a social issue. Remember, the editor doesn't solve the problem; they just publish your letter to create awareness.

fun_activity.title: 💌 Tone Switcher
fun_activity.instructions: Write one sentence asking for money formally (to a bank manager) and one sentence asking for money informally (to your best friend). Notice how the words completely change!

exam_tips: 📌 Write everything completely left-aligned (Block Format). Do not leave spaces before starting a paragraph.
📌 Never use an apostrophe in 'Yours'. It is 'Yours sincerely', NOT 'Your's sincerely'.
📌 Pay strict attention to the format marks. Even if your body text is weak, a perfect format will secure you guaranteed marks.
quick_recap: ⭐ The date should be written fully (e.g., 24 October 2024), not in numbers (24/10/24).
⭐ The body of a formal letter should have 3 paragraphs: Introduction of the problem, Details/Causes, and Suggestions/Expectations.
⭐ Informal letters end with warm closures like 'Yours lovingly' or 'With love'.
